title: Mathlib Imports
content: Imports natural and integer basics, finite sets with powerset operations, and general tactics. The powerset import is critical: subset sums and products are defined by iterating over $\text{Finset.powerset}(A)$ and mapping each subset to its sum or product.
mathContext: Requires $\text{Finset.powerset}$, $\text{Finset.image}$, $\text{Finset.sum}$, $\text{Finset.prod}$ for subset enumeration and aggregation.

title: Subset Sums
content: subsetSums A is the set of all integers of the form $\sum_{a \in S} a$ where $S \subseteq A$. It maps each element of $\text{powerset}(A)$ to its sum via $\text{Finset.image}$. The empty subset contributes $0$. For $|A| = n$, there are $2^n$ subsets but potentially far fewer distinct sums.

title: Subset Products
content: subsetProducts A is the set of all integers of the form $\prod_{a \in S} a$ where $S \subseteq A$ is nonempty. The nonempty filter avoids the trivial empty product. For a set of distinct primes, every nonempty subset gives a distinct product (unique factorization), so $|\text{subsetProducts}(A)| = 2^n - 1$.

title: Sums or Products
content: sumsOrProducts A is the union of subsetSums and subsetProducts — all integers representable via either operation on distinct elements. This is the central object of Problem 53: the question asks how large this set must be as a function of $|A|$.

title: Erdős Problem 53
content: The problem as a Lean Prop: for every $k \geq 1$, there exists $N_0$ such that for all $A$ with $|A| \geq N_0$, the number of representable integers $|\text{sumsOrProducts}(A)| \geq |A|^k$. This says the representable count grows faster than any polynomial in $|A|$, which is a strong form of 'arithmetic richness'.

title: Chang's Theorem (2003)
content: Mei-Chu Chang proved in 2003 that ErdosProblem53 holds: for every $k$, sufficiently large sets $A$ have at least $|A|^k$ representable integers as sums or products of distinct elements. Chang's proof combines the Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem (converting approximate additive structure to exact structure) with multiplicative energy estimates. The axiom asserts this as a fact, with the proof beyond the reach of current formal verification.
mathContext: $\text{chang\_theorem} : \text{ErdosProblem53}$; i.e., the polynomial lower bound holds for all $k$

title: Erdős-Szemerédi Upper Bound
content: Erdős and Szemerédi (1983) showed there exist arbitrarily large sets $A$ where the count of representable integers is at most $\exp(c (\log|A|)^2 \log\log|A|)$. This is subexponential in $\log|A|$ but super-polynomial, so the growth rate is pinched between polynomial (Chang's lower bound) and subexponential (this upper bound). The formalization approximates this with $|A|^{c \cdot (\log_2|A| + 1)}$ due to the difficulty of formalizing real exponentials.

title: Sum-Product Connection (Problem 52)
content: Problem 52 (the Erdős-Szemerédi sum-product conjecture) concerns pairwise operations: $|A + A| + |A \cdot A| \geq |A|^{2-\varepsilon}$. Problem 53 instead asks about subset operations (sums and products of distinct elements). The formalization defines sumset $A + A$ and productset $A \cdot A$ via Cartesian products, and states Problem 52 as a separate Prop. The two problems are deeply connected: both express the principle that a set cannot simultaneously have additive and multiplicative structure, but they measure different aspects of arithmetic richness.

title: Individual Counting Functions
content: subsetSumCount and subsetProductCount separately count the distinct integers representable as subset sums and subset products. The axioms assert that the union count $|\text{sumsOrProducts}(A)|$ is at least each individual count — a trivial consequence of $|X \cup Y| \geq \max(|X|, |Y|)$ for finite sets, but formalized explicitly for convenience.
